outline.subject: The Mannheim Observatory was a research facility in Germany that eventually relocated and evolved into the State Observatory Heidelberg-Königstuhl.

sections.title: Mannheim Observatory
sections.covers: This section provides an overview of the observatory's history, its relocation, and the current use of the original tower.

sections.title: Schwetzingen
sections.covers: This section describes the early astronomical activities and observations conducted by Christian Mayer at the court of Karl Theodor.

sections.title: The Palatinate Period
sections.covers: This section details the construction of the observatory in Mannheim and its development into an internationally recognized research institution.

sections.title: Christian Mayer’s Successors
sections.covers: This section outlines the challenges faced by the observatory under various directors and the damage sustained during the Napoleonic Era.

sections.title: The Baden Period
sections.covers: This section covers the decline of the observatory during the nineteenth century and the eventual decision to cease operations.

sections.title: Move to Karlsruhe
sections.covers: This section describes the final relocation of the observatory to Karlsruhe and its eventual integration into the new institution at Heidelberg.
